candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items); this item tests mobility, positioning, activities of daily living, and use of assistive/rehabilitation resources to maximize functional independence.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Mobility support, activities of daily living, and assistive rehabilitation after spinal cord injury
candidate.educational_objective: Support spinal cord injury rehabilitation through individualized, goal-directed mobility and functional care that maintains range of motion, promotes independence in activities of daily living, and coordinates appropriate rehabilitation and assistive resources.

options.A: Use an individualized rehabilitation plan that reflects the client's specific impairments, goals, and preferences and coordinate mobility, range-of-motion, and assistive-equipment needs with the rehabilitation team
options.B: Use the same mobility goals for every client with spinal cord injury because the level and pattern of impairment do not meaningfully change rehabilitation needs
options.C: Avoid mobility and range-of-motion activities until complete neurologic recovery is known with certainty
options.D: Treat mobility as exclusively a physical-therapy responsibility and omit nursing reinforcement of safe transfers, positioning, and daily functional activity

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current NICE rehabilitation guidance requires rehabilitation programmes to be tailored to the individual's needs and goals and to include appropriate physical and occupational therapies. For spinal cord injury specifically, NICE recommends maintaining joint range of motion, considering progressive sitting and other interventions to increase mobility, using specialised equipment when appropriate, and assessing assistive-technology needs without delay. NICE also recommends promoting independence in activities of daily living. B ignores the substantial variation in spinal cord injury impairments and needs. C delays rehabilitation without support. D incorrectly excludes nursing from coordinated mobility and functional care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current NICE guidance directly supports individualized, goal-based rehabilitation after spinal cord injury, maintenance of mobility and range of motion, promotion of functional independence, and coordinated use of assistive rehabilitation resources.
candidate.source_locator: NICE NG211 → Recommendation 1.5.1: rehabilitation programmes should be tailored to individual needs and goals and include appropriate physical/occupational therapies. Recommendation 1.11.9: promote independence with activities of daily living. Section 1.15 'Rehabilitation after spinal cord injury' → Recommendations 1.15.23–1.15.27: maintain joint range of motion; consider progressive sitting/tilt-table techniques to increase mobility; consider specialised equipment to promote mobility and independent walking; assess and refer for assistive technology without delay. Rationale and impact for maintaining mobility and movement: spinal cord injury disabilities and needs vary widely and mobility should be considered case by case.
candidate.source_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
candidate.source_version_date: NICE guideline NG211 published 2022-01-18; current guidance accessed 2026-08-18
candidate.stem: A client with a spinal cord injury is beginning rehabilitation. Which nursing approach best supports mobility and functional independence?
